subject.title: [Bug]: browser screenshot foregrounds the target tab on headed browsers (headless-only stall fix applied unconditionally)

question: For direct-CDP screenshots, should OpenClaw prefer non-activating capture with a one-time fresh-connection fallback, or preserve activation-first reliability when the browser's actual headless mode is unknown?
rationale: The current behavior was deliberately landed to fix a real headless stall, but it creates a deterministic headed-browser focus side effect; repository policy treats fallback behavior as a product decision, and source alone cannot choose the desired unknown-remote-session contract.

options.title: Capture first, reconnect on timeout
options.body: Try capture without activation and, only for the screenshot timeout, open a fresh socket, activate, and retry once.

options.title: Gate activation by known mode
options.body: Activate first only when the resolved browser mode is authoritatively headless, with an explicit rule for attached or remote unknown-mode endpoints.

options.title: Keep activation first
options.body: Retain the current reliability-first behavior and document that direct-CDP screenshots intentionally change the active tab.

recommendation.title: Capture first, reconnect on timeout
recommendation.body: Try capture without activation and, only for the screenshot timeout, open a fresh socket, activate, and retry once.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored and merged the intentional activation contract whose product tradeoff now needs reconsideration.
